proposed_widenings.name: create_illusion
proposed_widenings.justification: The Deck of Illusions creates a persistent visual illusion of a specific creature at a thrown card's location. This is fundamentally distinct from create_companion (real creature with physical substance): the illusion can do no harm, objects pass through it, and it is anchored to the card's position rather than moving under its own initiative. No existing effect atom captures 'create an insubstantial persistent illusion of a creature.'
proposed_widenings.evidence: An illusion of a creature, determined by rolling on the Deck of Illusions table, forms over the thrown card and remains until dispelled. The illusory creature created by the card looks and behaves like a real creature of its kind, except that it can do no harm... Any physical interaction with the illusory creature reveals it to be false, because objects pass through it.

proposed_widenings.name: move_illusion
proposed_widenings.justification: The owner can take a second Magic action to reposition the illusion within 30 feet of its card. This is a secondary activation that manipulates an already-existing illusion effect rather than creating a new creature or attachment. No existing atom models 'move an existing persistent illusion to a new position.'
proposed_widenings.evidence: While you are within 120 feet of the illusory creature and can see it, you can take a Magic action to move it anywhere within 30 feet of its card.

proposed_widenings.name: illusion_card_lifecycle
proposed_widenings.justification: The illusion is anchored to a physical card whose location bounds the illusion's position and whose state tracks whether the card has been consumed. When the card moves (or illusion is dispelled), both end simultaneously: the image on the card disappears and the card becomes permanently unusable. This card-anchored lifecycle — position-bound persistence, dual-end condition, and per-card destruction — has no existing model in the surface (companion dismissal, expire, or container_storage do not cover it).
proposed_widenings.evidence: The illusion lasts until its card is moved or the illusion is dispelled... When the illusion ends, the image on its card disappears, and that card can't be used again.

notes: The random_table ActivationPhase exists and could structurally host the d100 creature-selection table (33 outcome ranges). The activation family (MagicItemRecord + ActivatedAbilityMechanics) and charge_pool resource with permanent_on_empty destruction are also available. However, the core effect atom 'create_illusion' is entirely absent from v4 and the current TS surface. The closest existing atom (create_companion) models real, physically-present creatures — using it here would be a lie about the rule. The secondary move-illusion action and the card-anchored lifecycle compound the gap. No Dhall was authored because no honest encoding exists.
